in Santa Cruz, CA
Origins
2009
The Beginning
Redwoods, Santa Cruz
Tucked in the misty redwoods above Santa
Cruz, seven engineers gathered in a workshop.
They weren’t just building an aircraft. They were
chasing a dream. What if flight could be quiet, clean,
convenient — a part of everyday life?
Origins
2009
Imagine getting to work without traffic. Seeing your
city from the clouds. Saying “yes” to dinner across
town.
The sky shouldn’t be off limits. It should be a
shortcut. A sigh of relief. A daily moment of awe.
Because when you lift above the noise, everything
shifts — your view, your pace, your possibilities.
From the electric motors to airframes and
propellers, the aircraft was designed from the ground
up. It was slow, hands-on, and humbling. They started
over again and again. Relentlessly refining for reliability,
performance, and precision.
Origins
This wasn’t just a technical challenge. It meant
designing an entire ecosystem: infrastructure,
software, and service, all working in sync with the
cities we love.
The vision? To choreograph entire trips with just a
few taps, from ride-share to skyport to destination.
No gridlock. No stress. Just time, reclaimed.
Redwoods
What began as a dream in the trees has since
grown into a global effort to bring electric flight to life.
Because cleaner skies mean a healthier planet. Less
traffic means more time. And future generations
deserve both.

The Beginning

Day and night, a small team of seven engineers
work out of “The Barn,” our workshop in the
redwoods above Santa Cruz. We explore the
frontiers of technologies like electric motors,
flight software, and lithium-ion batteries,
engineering almost every component from the
ground up.
